campaigns.title: A qualified SQL object is one symbol, not one per name part

mutants.breaks: the defect exactly as it shipped: an `object_reference` holds one identifier per name part, so `public.orders` reports as TWO symbols and the index gains a chunk named after a schema. A test asserting `'public.orders' in symbols` would pass with both fragments still present, which is why the assertions are on the exact list

strict resolution `[agreed 2026-08-26]`. `orders` would resolve to `public.orders`, which is the bare-name matching that gives the knowledge graph its measured 48% ghost rate -- a name that looks unique is not the same as the right target. Re-pointed here on 2026-08-26: the first version aimed at a type guard in the SQL parser that turned out to be EQUIVALENT, because the query can only produce that node type. Strictness was never in the branch it named

campaigns.title: A Rust trait's members are symbols, and they carry the trait's name

mutants.breaks: the first of two causes. A trait's REQUIRED method is a `function_signature_item`, a different node type from `function_item` -- so the part of a trait that IS the contract had no symbol, no chunk and no node in the graph

the second cause, which is independent: a defaulted trait method was reported as the bare name `name`, colliding with every other `name` in the estate. Fixing only the query gives `Shape.area` unscoped; fixing only the scope leaves it missing

the branch order. In `impl Shape for C` both a trait and an impl are in scope and the method belongs to `C`; walking up finds the `impl_item` first. A walk that stopped at whichever it met without caring which would get every trait implementation backwards

campaigns.title: Indentation does not decide where code is cut

mutants.breaks: consistency across coding styles. Counting every character lets indentation decide where code is cut, so deeply nested Java and flat Python are judged by different standards for the same amount of code -- and reformatting a file moves its chunk boundaries without a line of it changing, which costs a re-index of the whole repository once anything is embedded
